title: Terraform fundamentals
subtitle: Choose provider versions and regions, and see how state connects them.

delta.before: Provider constraints often looked like an installation detail.
delta.after: Pin the provider version and check that its packages work on each platform you use.

exercises.title: Constraint Solver
exercises.description: Change a version constraint and see which provider versions it allows.

exercises.title: Lockfile Inspector
exercises.description: Work out why a provider package fails its checksum check.

cases.prompt: A lockfile initialized on macOS must support both Linux container architectures.
choices: Search for a linux label in each hash
Run providers lock with explicit -platform options
cases.correct: Run providers lock with explicit -platform options
cases.explanation: Generate checksums for linux_amd64, linux_arm64 and darwin_arm64, then test readonly initialization.

cases.prompt: An allowed newer provider exists, but the committed lockfile still selects 5.92.0.
choices: init always selects the newest version
init respects the compatible locked version
cases.correct: init respects the compatible locked version
cases.explanation: An explicit init -upgrade considers new allowed versions.

cost.assumptions: Short-lived resources, no compute, standard parameters, no uploads; gross usage before account credits.

checkpoints.prompt: Which constraint allows AWS 5.92.0 but remains below 6.0?

rationale.a: It allows the remainder of the 5.x series from 5.80 onward.

checkpoints.prompt: How does a resource select the UK AWS configuration, and which component makes its AWS API calls?

choices.a: provider = aws.uk; the AWS provider plugin makes the API calls
choices.b: region = aws.uk; Terraform core replaces the AWS plugin

rationale.a: The meta-argument routes to the alias, and the plugin implements provider API interactions.
rationale.b: A resource region argument is not the provider selector, and core does not replace the provider API implementation.

checkpoints.prompt: Does state replace the need to keep desired configuration?

rationale.a: State tracks associations and observations; it is not desired configuration.
rationale.b: Both configuration and state serve distinct purposes.
